title: Maximum Number of Groups Entering a Competition
summary: Given a positive integer array representing student grades, determine the maximum number of non-empty groups that can be formed such that each subsequent group has a greater sum of grades and a larger number of students than the previous group.
statement: Given a positive integer array representing student grades, determine the maximum number of non-empty groups that can be formed such that each subsequent group has a greater sum of grades and a larger number of students than the previous group.
constraints: Use every student in at most one group; grade values may be assigned in any order.
Each next group must have strictly more students and a strictly larger grade sum than the previous group.
Return the maximum possible number of groups.
reference_solution:
def maximum_increasing_competition_groups(grades):
    groups=0;used=0;n=len(grades)
    while used+groups+1<=n:groups+=1;used+=groups
    return groups
known_wrong_solutions:

def maximum_increasing_competition_groups(grades):
    groups=0;used=0;n=len(grades)
    while used+groups+1<=n:groups+=1;used+=groups+1
    return groups
hints: Only the number of available students limits the group count because positive grades can be ordered to make sums rise with group size.
The smallest strictly increasing group sizes are one, two, ..., g.
Increase g while the triangular total g(g+1)/2 fits within n students.
Any g groups need at least that many students, and assigning sorted grades across those growing sizes realizes increasing sums, so the bound is tight.
editorial: Any g groups need at least that many students, and assigning sorted grades across those growing sizes realizes increasing sums, so the bound is tight.

tests.explanation: Six students can form groups of sizes one, two, and three with increasing grade sums.
Two students cannot form two groups of sizes one and two, so only one group is possible.
